name: Tai Daeng-Meuay
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog cites only Pittayaporn 2009 and Chamberlain 1975 (classification); no descriptive grammar/phonology of Tai Daeng located

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page taid1249 and Hammarström hh.bib entries with lgcode [tyr] (local copy.
sources.note: Bibliographic records only. Works tagged for tyr: Ferlus 2008 (phonology), Gedney 1964 (comparative phonology sketch), Hudak 1994 (Gedney's SW Tai glossaries incl. 3 Red Tai dialects), Robert 1941 (ethnography/wordlist/text), Pacquement 2022 (overview), Chamberlain 1984 (comparative overview), Jonsson 1991, Robinson 1994, Onlao 2010 (thesis + article), Soutthixay 2016-17/2019-20 (Lao MA theses, wordlist/text), Degeorge 1927-28 (proverbs), Anonymous 2004 (Nakai wordlist), Schliesinger 2003, Bradley 2007.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 2008. "The Tai dialects of Nghệ An, Vietnam (Tay Daeng, Tay Yo, Tay Muong)". In Diller, Edmondson & Luo (eds), The Tai-Kadai Languages, London/New York: Routledge, 298-315. Author's updated French version (2017) 'Les dialectes tai du Nghệ An, Vietnam (Tay Daeng, Tay Yo, Tay Muong)', HAL halshs-01617791, 24 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey); publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Sec. 3 'Généralités phonétiques' (p. 4 of HAL version) states the basic word in Tay Daeng, Tay Yo and Tay Muong is strictly monosyllabic CV(C)/T; sec. 4 (pp. 4-6) gives Tay Daeng consonants, vowels (length contrast), and 5- or 6-tone systems for Con Cuông, Mai Châu Thượng and Mai Châu Hạ. Grep for accent/tonique/intensité/proéminence/stress: no hits.
Phonology section gives syllable structure and 5 tones on free / 2 on checked syllables, citing Gedney (1989) and Pacquement (2021); no statement on stress.

sources.citation: Onlao, Sasithorn. 2010. การจัดกลุ่มภาษาไทในลุ่มน้ำพาว เมืองคำเกิด แขวงบอลิคำไซ สปป.ลาว โดยใช้เกณฑ์การเปลี่ยนแปลงร่วมกันของเสียงวรรณยุกต์ [Grouping of Tai languages in Nam Paw basin, Khamkeut District, Bolikhamxai Province, Lao PDR, by criteria of tonal sound changes]. Journal of Mekong Societies 6(3): 47-72.
sources.note: Tone systems only (Gedney-box splits/mergers) for Tai-thaeng, Tai-mot, Tai-moei (= Tai Meuay, tyr), Phu Tai, Nyo and Lao; no mention of stress (grep for น้ำหนัก/เน้น/stress: no hits).

sources.citation: Pittayaporn, Pittayawat. 2009. The Phonology of Proto-Tai. PhD dissertation, Cornell University (eCommons 1813/13855), 438 pp.
sources.note: Comparative reconstruction (Proto-Tai as sesquisyllabic with iambic prosodic words); grep finds no Tai Daeng / Red Tai / Mai Châu data at all, so it says nothing about Tai Daeng stress. Cited by Glottolog only for classification.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 1999. "Les dialectes et les écritures des Tai (Thai) du Nghệ An (Vietnam)". Treizièmes Journées de Linguistique d'Asie Orientale, Paris (EHESS-CNRS), 10-11 June 1999. HAL halshs-00927749, 22 pp. (image-only PDF, scanned with tesseract eng at 150 dpi).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Covers ethnonyms, informants (Tai Deng of Mai Châu, Tai Thanh of Con Cuông), comparative initials, tones and the scripts; the only 'accent' hits in the scanned text concern Siamese script tone marks.

sources.citation: Pacquement, Jean. 2022. "The Tai Meuay of Bolikhamxay Province (Laos), their ethnonym, and their language". In Mark J. Alves & Paul Sidwell (eds), Studies in the Anthropology of Language in Mainland Southeast Asia, JSEALS Special Publication 8, 33-55. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press.

sources.note: Most recent first-hand description of the Lao (Tai Meuay) variety of tyr; JSEALS special publications are open access but the volume could not be located from our machine.

sources.citation: Onlao, Sasithorn. 2010. The Grouping of Tai Language in Nam Paw Basin, Khamkeut District, Bolikhamxai Province, Lao PDR. MA thesis, Mahasarakham University (Thai).
